chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Sayf al-Tammar, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'A man says to his wife,
You are unto me like the back of my sister, or my paternal aunt, or my maternal aunt.
He (peace be upon him) said: 'Allah has only mentioned the mothers, and in this is the prohibition.'

key_terms.الزَّهَار: Zuhar; a pre-Islamic form of divorce where a man likened his wife to his mother, making her unlawful to him without expiation.
key_terms.الظَّهْر: The back; used in the phrase 'like the back of my mother' to denote a specific type of divorce/prohibition.
key_terms.الْأُمَّهَاتِ: The mothers; the specific category mentioned in the Quranic verse regarding Zuhar.
key_terms.حَرَامٌ: Forbidden; indicating the legal status of the act described.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a man saying to his wife 'You are like my mother's back' in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the Quranic term 'mothers' in Surah Al-Mujadila is not limited to biological mothers but serves as a comprehensive category for all close female relatives, such as sisters and aunts. This interpretation establishes that the specific legal mechanism of *Zuhar*—which requires expiation for divorcing a wife—applies whenever a man uses similar phrasing regarding any of these kin, thereby extending the pre-Islamic practice's regulation to a broader familial context.

en.hubeali:
Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan, from Sayf Al Tammar who said, 
‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘The man is saying to his wife, ‘You are unto me like the back of my sister’, or ‘my paternal aunt’, or ‘my maternal aunt’.
So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘But rather, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mentioned the ‘mothers’, and in this is the Prohibition’.
en.sarwar: 18. Abu Ali al-Ash‘ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan from Sayf al-Tammar who has said the following:
“I once asked abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who says to his wife, ‘
You are like the back of my sister, maternal or paternal aunt.’
He (the Imam) said, ‘Allah has mentioned the mothers, this certainly is unlawful. ’”
